title: Federated Brief Contract
summary: Host-neutral read-only federation of independently published Shin indexes with per-member freshness, local-rank fusion, bounded global evidence, and source provenance.

command.name: federated-brief
command.syntax: shin-context federated-brief --config FILE QUERY [--limit N] [--per-doc N] [--require-current]
command.globalSingleProfileOptions: --profile, --profile-dir, --root, --out-dir, --from-index, and --source-scan are rejected; all member locations come from the federation config

config.pathResolution: Relative profileDir, root, and outDir values resolve against the federation config directory, independent of process cwd.
config.ordering: Member array order has no authority meaning; runtime order is stable member id order.

limits.materializedRecords: At most members multiplied by the global evidence limit; each member retains the existing 20000-row generated-index candidate ceiling.

snapshotAndLocking.lockProtocol: Canonical outDir paths are sorted and shared index locks are acquired in that order before any member freshness or retrieval work.
snapshotAndLocking.lockLifetime: FederationSession owns the complete shared lock set. federated-brief holds it through final JSON emission; federated-eval holds it across every suite case and releases it before report emission.
snapshotAndLocking.boundary: The command observes one stable published snapshot per member but does not claim a distributed transaction or one cross-repository source timestamp.
snapshotAndLocking.memberSnapshotId: Each member snapshot_id is the same active-manifest identity emitted by that member's local generated-index search, context, brief, and eval commands.
snapshotAndLocking.snapshotSetId: Deterministic FNV identity over federation id, sorted member ids, profiles, and generated manifest snapshots; it is a drift identity, not a cryptographic authenticity proof.
snapshotAndLocking.publicationGuard: Every member publication-in-progress marker is checked after the shared lock set is acquired; incomplete publication fails closed before freshness or retrieval.

freshness.normal: Every member runs the existing complete normal freshness contract; aggregate current and fully_verified are conjunctions across members.
freshness.requireCurrent: --require-current performs exact generated-output verification for every member and fails the complete command when any member is stale.
freshness.profileSnapshot: Profile bytes are hashed when the profile is loaded so generation and freshness use the parsed configuration snapshot rather than rereading changed bytes later.

nonGoals: no product-specific routing or implicit repository discovery
no remote service, daemon, MCP, ACL, or distributed lock
no cross-profile comparison of raw retrieval scores
verification: Use arbitrary synthetic member roots, including denied, missing, stale, and valid publications.

retrieval.memberPipeline: Each member independently runs its profile aliases, strict/scoped/relaxed/planned brief pipeline and local global evidence selector.
rankFusion: Raw scores are never compared as cross-profile authority because profile aliases, topics, and planned boosts are local.
Cross-member ordering uses local_rank ascending, matched query group count descending, strict before fallback, evidence type, member id, path, line, and stable id.
The global selector seeds non-empty evidence types before filling the remaining budget from rank-fused candidates.
deduplication: Cross-member deduplication requires the same canonical relative source path, generated content hash, byte count, evidence type, evidence_kind, verification_level, and canonical row payload.
Records without generated source identity are namespaced by member and are never deduplicated across members.
A deduplicated record retains sorted member_ids; duplicate appearances never improve local rank.

result.configHash: federation.config_hash is a semantic FNV identity over sorted resolved member ids, profiles, profile directories, roots, and output roots; declaration order and JSON formatting do not affect it.
